verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents its own controls for session lifetime and refresh tokens. Access-token expiry is configurable via the 'JWT expiry limit' setting, and refresh token rotation detects reuse of revoked refresh tokens. Nothing shows an explicit, immediate server-side way to kill a compromised session, and the access JWT is not shown to be invalidated before it expires. missing for 10: documented immediate server-side session/access-token revocation (e.g., admin sign-out or revoke-session API), detail on multi-device session termination, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage session lifecycle — expiry, refresh, and immediate server-side revocation of a compromised session

citations.quote: Control session lifetime, refresh tokens, and multi-device sign-in behavior.
The expiry of an access token can be set in the "JWT expiry limit" field in [your project's auth settings]
If refresh token rotation is enabled, auth will automatically detect malicious attempts to reuse a revoked refresh token.
